vulns.name: Log4Shell
vulns.discoverer: Chen Zhaojun, Alibaba Cloud Security Team
vulns.summary: Log4j 2 resolved ${jndi:...} lookups inside logged strings, so any attacker-controlled text that got logged (a User-Agent header, a username, a chat message) could make the server fetch and run a Java class from an attacker's LDAP or RMI server. Because Log4j is embedded in a huge number of Java products and services, it was one of the most widespread critical vulnerabilities ever disclosed. Several follow-up CVEs fixed incomplete patches and related lookup flaws.
vulns.affected: log4j-core 2.0-beta9 through 2.14.1 for CVE-2021-44228; follow-on CVEs extend the range up to 2.17.0 (excluding the 2.3.x/2.12.x security releases)
vulns.fixed: 2.17.1 (Java 8+), 2.12.4 (Java 7), 2.3.2 (Java 6) fix all four CVEs. 2.15.0 was the first fix for CVE-2021-44228, 2.16.0 for CVE-2021-45046, and 2.17.0 for CVE-2021-45105
vulns.mitigation: Upgrade log4j-core to 2.17.1 / 2.12.4 / 2.3.2 or later. Early workarounds such as formatMsgNoLookups proved insufficient; the only stopgap Apache endorsed was removing the JndiLookup class from the classpath.

cves.note: JNDI lookup in log messages lets an attacker load remote code (the original Log4Shell). KEV 2021-12-10, known ransomware use.
Incomplete 2.15.0 fix; Thread Context (MDC) lookups in non-default patterns allow RCE or info leak. Fixed in 2.16.0. KEV 2023-05-01.
Uncontrolled recursion from self-referential lookups causes DoS. Fixed in 2.17.0. Not in KEV.
RCE via JDBC Appender with a JNDI LDAP data source; requires an attacker who can change the logging config. Fixed in 2.17.1. Not in KEV.

real_world.headline: Within days of disclosure attackers were probing nearly half of the world's corporate networks, and nation-state APTs, the Conti ransomware gang and cryptominers were still using Log4Shell to break in years later.
real_world.exposure: Google counted 35,863 Maven Central artifacts (over 8% of the repository) depending on vulnerable Log4j, and the CSRB said the flaw touched 'virtually every networked organization'.

events.text: CISA added CVE-2021-44228 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, with a December 24 federal patch deadline; the catalog flags it as used in ransomware campaigns.
Microsoft reported mass scanning, coin miners and Cobalt Strike, and later added nation-state groups including PHOSPHORUS (Iran) and HAFNIUM (China) to its list of actors exploiting the flaw.
Check Point said it had blocked more than 4.3 million exploitation attempts, 46% of them from known malicious groups, and had seen attempted exploits against over 48% of corporate networks worldwide.
CISA issued Emergency Directive 22-02, ordering federal civilian agencies to patch or mitigate Log4j on their internet-facing systems.
AdvIntel reported that the Conti ransomware gang was using Log4Shell to move laterally to VMware vCenter servers.

Belgium's Ministry of Defence confirmed that a Log4j exploit had breached its network and paralyzed some of its activities for several days, the first NATO defence ministry publicly hit through the flaw.
The FTC warned that it would take legal action against companies that failed to remediate Log4j, citing its $700M Equifax settlement.

The Cyber Safety Review Board's first report called Log4j an 'endemic vulnerability' likely to persist for a decade or more, and noted that one cabinet department had spent 33,000 hours on its response.

CISA and the FBI disclosed that Iranian government-sponsored actors had used Log4Shell in an unpatched VMware Horizon server to breach a federal civilian agency, where they deployed XMRig, Mimikatz and Ngrok.
Cisco Talos reported that North Korea's Lazarus/Andariel was still exploiting Log4Shell in VMware Horizon two years on, using it to deploy the new NineRAT and DLRAT malware ('Operation Blacksmith').

vulns.name: Spring4Shell
vulns.discoverer: codeplutos and meizjm3i of AntGroup FG Security Lab (secondary report from Praetorian)
vulns.summary: Spring's data binding let request parameters reach class.module.classLoader on JDK 9+. On Tomcat, attackers could use this to rewrite the access-log settings and drop a JSP web shell. It bypassed the 2010 fix for CVE-2010-1622, and details and a PoC leaked publicly before the patch.
vulns.affected: Spring Framework 5.3.0-5.3.17, 5.2.0-5.2.19 and older unsupported versions; the known exploit needs JDK 9+, Apache Tomcat, WAR deployment, and spring-webmvc or spring-webflux
vulns.fixed: Spring Framework 5.3.18 and 5.2.20 (Spring Boot 2.6.6 / 2.5.12 pull in the fix)
vulns.mitigation: Upgrade Spring Framework (or Spring Boot). If you cannot upgrade yet, upgrade Tomcat (10.0.20 / 9.0.62 / 8.5.78), downgrade to Java 8, or add a disallowedFields binder for class.* / Class.* patterns, as Spring's early announcement describes.

cves.note: Spring MVC/WebFlux RCE via data binding on JDK 9+ (Spring4Shell). KEV 2022-04-04.

A separate, unrelated bug: SpEL injection via the spring.cloud.function.routing-expression header in Spring Cloud Function <=3.1.6 / <=3.2.2 (fixed 3.1.7 / 3.2.3). Disclosed the same week and often grouped or confused with Spring4Shell, but it is not Spring4Shell. KEV 2022-08-25.

vulns.name: Text4Shell
vulns.discoverer: Alvaro Munoz (GitHub Security Lab)
vulns.summary: Apache Commons Text's StringSubstitutor turned on the 'script', 'dns' and 'url' lookups by default. If untrusted input reached a default interpolator, a string like ${script:javascript:...} could run code on the server. The bug class resembles Log4Shell, but real-world exposure was much smaller because applications rarely pass untrusted input to these APIs.
vulns.impact: RCE (only when untrusted input reaches StringSubstitutor interpolation with default lookups)
vulns.affected: Apache Commons Text 1.5 through 1.9
vulns.fixed: Apache Commons Text 1.10.0 (problematic lookups disabled by default)
vulns.mitigation: Upgrade to Commons Text 1.10.0 or later. Do not pass untrusted input to StringSubstitutor.createInterpolator() or to the default lookups.

cves.note: Default script/dns/url interpolators in StringSubstitutor allow code execution or remote contact. Not in KEV.

vulns.name: React2Shell
vulns.product: React Server Components (react-server-dom-webpack / -parcel / -turbopack) and frameworks built on them, notably Next.js App Router
vulns.discoverer: Lachlan Davidson (reported to Meta Bug Bounty on 2025-11-29)
vulns.summary: React Server Components unsafely deserialized 'Flight' protocol payloads sent to Server Function endpoints. One crafted HTTP request could therefore run code on the server, with no login and often in a default Next.js App Router app. Public exploits appeared within a day or two, and CISA added it to KEV on 2025-12-05 after China-nexus groups began exploiting it. Follow-up research found DoS and source-code-exposure bugs in the same code, none of them RCE.
vulns.affected: react-server-dom-* 19.0.0, 19.1.0, 19.1.1, 19.2.0; Next.js 15.x, 16.x and 14.3.0-canary.77+ (App Router). Also react-router RSC, waku, @parcel/rsc, @vitejs/plugin-rsc, rwsdk. Next.js 13.x, 14.x stable, Pages Router and Edge Runtime are not affected
vulns.fixed: RCE fixed in React 19.0.1 / 19.1.2 / 19.2.1 and Next.js 15.0.5, 15.1.9, 15.2.6, 15.3.6, 15.4.8, 15.5.7, 16.0.7. React 19.0.4 / 19.1.5 / 19.2.4 also fix the follow-on DoS and source-exposure CVEs (including CVE-2026-23864, Jan 2026)
vulns.mitigation: Upgrade React RSC packages and your framework to the latest patched release (for Next.js, `npx fix-react2shell-next`). There is no workaround, and WAF rules are only temporary. Vercel recommends rotating secrets for any app that was online and unpatched on 2025-12-04.

cves.note: Pre-auth RCE via unsafe deserialization in RSC Server Function endpoints (React2Shell). KEV 2025-12-05, known ransomware use per KEV.
Next.js-specific CVE (GHSA-9qr9-h5gf-34mp), rejected as a duplicate of CVE-2025-55182.
Source code exposure: a crafted request can return a Server Function's source when an argument is stringified. Disclosed 2025-12-11, reported by Andrew MacPherson.
Pre-auth DoS: an infinite loop during deserialization hangs the server. Disclosed 2025-12-11, reported by RyotaK (GMO Flatt Security) and Shinsaku Nomura.
Incomplete fix for CVE-2025-55184 (DoS) in 19.0.2 / 19.1.3 / 19.2.2. Found internally by the React team and disclosed 2025-12-11.

events.text: React disclosed the CVSS 10.0 pre-auth RCE in the React Server Components Flight protocol, which also affects Next.js and other RSC frameworks; Wiz found vulnerable versions in up to 39% of cloud environments.
AWS reported exploitation within hours of disclosure from infrastructure tied to the China state-nexus groups Earth Lamia and Jackpot Panda.
CISA added CVE-2025-55182 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; the catalog now flags it as used in ransomware campaigns.
S-RM saw React2Shell used as initial access for Weaxor ransomware (a suspected Mallox rebrand), which encrypted the server less than a minute after the break-in.

vulns.name: PHP2Shell
vulns.discoverer: Calif Research (Ryan Austin), Wiz Research (Sagi Tzadik et al.), and OpenAI; GHSA also credits reporter tomash-areion
vulns.summary: Two memory-safety bugs in PHP's core request lifecycle. One leaves request memory uninitialized when an out-of-memory error aborts a request, and the other leaves global state pointing at freed request memory. Either can be triggered with crafted multipart or session-upload-progress requests and turned into unauthenticated remote code execution in the PHP worker.
vulns.affected: All PHP versions before 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12 that serve web requests, with mod_php at highest risk. EOL branches (back to at least 5.4 per Wiz) are also affected.
vulns.fixed: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35 (2026-10-21); the PHP security team published source backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1
vulns.mitigation: Upgrade immediately; PHP says no mitigation is complete. Interim hardening: memory_limit=-1, a low post_max_size and session.upload_progress.enabled=0, plus WAF rules.

cves.note: RCE via OOM corruption: longjmp() on out-of-memory leaves request memory uninitialized and request shutdown then uses it (CWE-416). NVD's CVSS 3.1 score is 9.8.
RCE via stale global state: worker globals still point into freed request memory and the next request uses them, e.g. the session.upload_progress path (CWE-416). NVD's CVSS 3.1 score is 8.1.

vulns.name: Node2Shell
vulns.product: Google Brotli decoder (bundled in Node.js, Python Brotli/brotlicffi, .NET, Bun, Envoy, and others)
vulns.discoverer: OpenAI Codex Security (Khai Tran and Sylvie Mayer), per the Node.js advisory; Imperva Red Team (Ron Masas) did the RCE research
vulns.summary: An out-of-bounds write in Google's Brotli decoder. An invalid block switch was reported as 'needs more input' instead of a format error, so the streaming decoder kept writing past an 8-byte internal buffer. Any software that decompresses attacker-supplied Brotli data, such as HTTP request or response bodies with Content-Encoding: br, can crash, leak memory or, on some builds, run attacker code.
vulns.impact: Unauthenticated RCE (memory corruption, info disclosure, DoS); exploitability depends on the build and whether the app decodes untrusted Brotli
vulns.affected: Google Brotli 1.0.3 through 1.2.0. Node.js 22.x/24.x/26.x before the fixes, plus EOL 20/23/25 with no fix. PyPI Brotli >=1.0.3,<1.2.1 and brotlicffi >=1.0.3,<1.2.1.0. .NET 8/9/10 (11 RC), where exposure needs Brotli decompression to be enabled. Also Bun, Envoy, PAN-OS, Apple OSes and vendored copies.
vulns.mitigation: Update every Brotli copy (runtime, language packages, container images, vendored libraries) and restart services. Until then, reject or strip Content-Encoding: br request bodies at the proxy or WAF, and turn off Brotli decompression in .NET or Express where it is not needed.

cves.note: Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) out-of-bounds write via an unchecked return value (CWE-252/CWE-787). NVD's CVSS 3.1 score is 9.8. Node.js rates it High and Microsoft's .NET advisory gives CVSS 3.1 8.1.

vulns.name: wp2shell
vulns.discoverer: Adam Kues (Assetnote / Searchlight Cyber); the CVE-2026-60137 SQLi was also independently reported by TF1T, dtro and haongo
vulns.summary: wp2shell is a pre-authentication remote code execution chain in a stock WordPress install with no plugins. A route-confusion bug in the REST API batch endpoint (/wp-json/batch/v1) lets an anonymous attacker reach a SQL injection in WP_Query's author__not_in parameter. From there the attacker takes over an admin account and uploads a malicious plugin to run code.
vulns.affected: WordPress 6.9.0-6.9.4, 7.0.0-7.0.1 and 7.1 beta1 (full chain); 6.8.0-6.8.5 affected by CVE-2026-60137 only; versions before 6.8 not affected
vulns.fixed: 7.0.2, 6.9.5, 6.8.6 (SQLi only), 7.1 beta2; released 2026-07-17 with forced auto-updates
vulns.mitigation: Update to 7.0.2 / 6.9.5 (or 6.8.6) right away. WordPress.org pushed forced auto-updates. If you cannot patch, temporarily block anonymous access to /wp-json/batch/v1 and ?rest_route=/batch/v1 at the WAF; Cloudflare shipped managed WAF rules.

cves.note: REST API batch endpoint route confusion that exposes the author__not_in SQLi to unauthenticated users and leads to RCE (KEV: 'Interpretation Conflict')

real_world.exposure: Wiz found that 60% of organizations running WordPress had a vulnerable instance at disclosure and 25% exposed one to the internet, falling to 50% and 10% within 24 hours.

events.text: Searchlight Cyber (Assetnote) disclosed wp2shell, a no-plugin, no-auth RCE chain in WordPress 6.9 to 7.0.1; WordPress shipped 6.9.5 and 7.0.2 and pushed forced auto-updates.

KEVIntel tracked broad scanning, and one actor was seen repeatedly trying to install the Go-based Overlord RAT.

vulns.name: Plex2Shell
vulns.discoverer: Zach Main (zmain / code-zm)
vulns.summary: Plex2Shell chains four Plex Media Server bugs into unauthenticated code execution. An SSRF in /player/timeline accepts any X-Plex-Token value. The attacker uses it to reach the loopback-only plugin API and steal the owner's admin token. With that token, the attacker writes a malicious shared library into the Codecs directory, and Plex loads it unsigned and runs it as the plex user. The chain was exploited from 2026-10-17, one day after the PoC was published, to install XMRig miners and proxyware.
vulns.impact: Unauthenticated RCE (as the Plex service user)
vulns.affected: Plex Media Server before 1.43.3.10861 (Plex's advisory says v1.43.2 and earlier)
vulns.fixed: Plex Media Server 1.43.3.10861 (shipped ~2026-08-03/04; Plex security notice posted 2026-09-01)
vulns.mitigation: Update Plex Media Server to 1.43.3.10861 or later and do not expose port 32400 directly to the internet. Treat any internet-reachable server on an older build as possibly compromised: check the Codecs directory for unexpected .so/.dll files, look for miner or proxy processes, and rotate the Plex account token.

cves.note: SSRF via /player/timeline 'protocol' parameter; any X-Plex-Token value accepted (CVSS 4.0: 5.3)
URL values in 'searchOne' not neutralized, so the attacker can call other plugins' functions with their own parameters (CVSS 4.0: 6.9)
SSRF via /video/:/transcode/universal path parameter (CVSS 4.0: 5.3)

vulns.name: NGINX2Shell
vulns.discoverer: Found independently by Wiz Research (Nir Ohfeld, Tomer Schwartz), Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7 (Stephen Fewer) and Xint
vulns.summary: CVE-2026-123007 is an integer underflow in NGINX's HTTP/2 flow control. Cancelling a stream with data still queued returns unused window back to send_window without capping it at the maximum. A later unsigned bounds check then wraps, and a negative length reaches an out-of-bounds heap copy in the TLS send path, which can lead to remote code execution in the worker process. It shipped together with a second HTTP/2 RCE-class bug, CVE-2026-123633 (a use-after-free), and three more memory-safety fixes in nginx 1.31.9 / 1.30.7.
vulns.impact: Unauthenticated RCE (worker process); DoS at minimum
vulns.affected: NGINX Open Source 1.9.5-1.31.8 with HTTP/2 enabled (CVE-2026-123633: 1.19.7+); NGINX Plus R33 through 37.x before fixed builds (R34-R36 have no fix listed); F5 NGINX Ingress Controller before 5.8.0; forks such as OpenResty, Tengine, Angie and freenginx reportedly contain the code
vulns.mitigation: Upgrade to nginx 1.31.9 / 1.30.7 (or a fixed NGINX Plus build), then do a full restart, because a reload keeps old workers running. If you cannot patch, disable HTTP/2 with 'http2 off;' on 1.25.1+ or by removing 'http2' from listen directives.

cves.note: HTTP/2 flow-control window integer underflow leading to heap out-of-bounds write; F5 also scores CVSS 4.0 9.2 (Critical); nginx.org severity 'major'

vulns.name: Java4Shell
vulns.discoverer: Quang Luong (Calif.io); Oracle also credits Albert Yang
vulns.summary: A heap overflow in the AVX-512 VBMI-accelerated Base64 decoder intrinsic of the HotSpot JVM on x86-64. Any Java app that Base64-decodes attacker-controlled input can have its heap corrupted, crashing the JVM or potentially leading to code execution. Details leaked shortly before the coordinated Oracle/OpenJDK release on 17 Nov 2026.
vulns.impact: Unauthenticated remote code execution or JVM crash (DoS); Calif demonstrated pre-auth RCE in default Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate and post-auth RCE in Kafka, Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit and Spinnaker. Datadog and OX Security note DoS is far easier than reliable RCE.
vulns.affected: OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later on the 17, 21, 25 and 27 lines (and downstream builds: Corretto, Temurin, Zulu, Liberica, Microsoft, Red Hat, SapMachine, GraalVM), only on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (Intel Ice Lake+ Xeon, AMD Zen 4+). Oracle lists Java SE 8u511b33-perf, 17.0.21.0.3, 21.0.13.0.3, 25.0.5.0.3, 27.0.1.0.3; GraalVM for JDK 17.0.21.0.3/21.0.13.0.3; GraalVM EE 21.3.20.0.3. ARM64 and standard Java 8/11 not affected.
vulns.fixed: Oracle/OpenJDK 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1, 27.0.1.1, 8u513-perf; GraalVM 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 21.3.20.1; Amazon Corretto 27.0.1.1.4 (and siblings) and Azul Zulu shipped 17 Nov; Temurin rolling out; Red Hat/Ubuntu fixes pending as of 18 Nov.
vulns.mitigation: Update to a fixed JDK build and restart all JVMs, including bundled runtimes and container images. As a stopgap start the JVM with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics (or -XX:UseAVX=2 on x86-64 only).

cves.note: Heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-122/787) in HotSpot x86-64 AVX-512 VBMI Base64 decode intrinsic. Oracle CVSS 3.1 8.1 (AC:H); Calif CVSS 4.0 9.2; Red Hat preliminary 9.8.

vulns.discoverer: Independent researcher Sean Bales (GitHub: MSPNightmare); CVE-2026-125882 also credited to Nate Fair (Sprocket Security)

vulns.name: KindaRails2Shell
vulns.product: Ruby on Rails (Active Storage with libvips)
vulns.discoverer: André Baptista, Bruno Mendes and Rafael Castilho (Ethiack); independently RyotaK (GMO Flatt Security)
vulns.summary: Rails Active Storage never told libvips to block its unsafe loaders, so a crafted image upload can make libvips read arbitrary files on the server. Leaking secrets like secret_key_base can then be escalated to remote code execution. Ethiack named it 'Kinda' because the chain needs a few common-but-not-universal conditions.
vulns.impact: Unauthenticated arbitrary file read as the Rails process, leading to secret theft and possible RCE / lateral movement.
vulns.affected: Rails 7.0.0-7.2.3.1, 8.0.0-8.0.5, 8.1.0-8.1.3 using Active Storage with the Vips processor and accepting untrusted uploads; Rails 6.0-6.1 in non-default Vips configs. ImageMagick backend not affected.
vulns.fixed: Rails 7.2.3.2, 8.0.5.1, 8.1.3.1 plus libvips 8.13+ (and ruby-vips 2.2.1+).
vulns.mitigation: Upgrade Rails and libvips, then rotate secret_key_base and other app secrets. Stopgap: set VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED or call Vips.block_untrusted(true) on libvips 8.13+, and run the rails-forensics tool to check for abuse.

cves.note: Active Storage does not disable unsafe libvips operations, allowing arbitrary file read via crafted upload (GHSA-xr9x-r78c-5hrm)

vulns.name: Plugin4Shell
vulns.product: AI coding agent plugin installers (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI)
vulns.discoverer: Or Nevo, Dor Granat and Niv Hoffman (Air Security research lab)
vulns.summary: Four popular AI coding agents asked git for a plugin's pinned commit SHA but never checked that the checked-out HEAD actually matched it. A plugin owner could create a branch named after the reviewed commit hash so git resolved the branch tip instead, swapping in attacker code while the pin still looked valid. Background plugin auto-updates re-ran the checkout, so no user action was needed once a plugin was installed.
vulns.impact: Zero-click code execution via plugin supply chain (SHA-pin bypass)

vulns.fixed: Claude Code 2.1.179; Codex 0.146.0; VS Code 1.136.0 (Copilot); Gemini CLI will not be fixed (deprecated in favour of Antigravity)
vulns.mitigation: Update each agent; where an agent cannot be patched, disable automatic plugin updates and only source plugins from hosts that reject SHA-shaped branch names; independently verify the commit each plugin resolves to.

vulns.name: ProxyShell
vulns.discoverer: Orange Tsai (DEVCORE)
vulns.summary: ProxyShell chains three Exchange bugs: a pre-auth path confusion in the Client Access Service (CVE-2021-34473), an elevation of privilege in the Exchange PowerShell backend (CVE-2021-34523) and an arbitrary file write via mailbox export (CVE-2021-31207). Together they let an unauthenticated attacker drop a web shell on the server. Microsoft patched it quietly in April and May 2021, and mass exploitation followed within about a week of Orange Tsai's Black Hat talk.
vulns.affected: Exchange Server 2013, 2016 and 2019 without the April/May 2021 security updates
vulns.fixed: April 2021 (KB5001779) and May 2021 (KB5003435) Exchange security updates and later CUs
vulns.mitigation: Install current Exchange CUs and security updates; hunt for web shells and suspicious mailbox exports; keep Exchange off direct internet exposure where possible.

vulns.name: ProxyNotShell
vulns.discoverer: GTSC (Vietnam), via Trend Micro ZDI
vulns.summary: ProxyNotShell pairs an SSRF in Exchange (CVE-2022-41040) with a remote code execution bug reachable through Exchange PowerShell remoting (CVE-2022-41082). It looked like ProxyShell, but needs any valid mailbox credentials, which is how it got the 'Not' in its name. It was exploited as a zero-day before disclosure, and Microsoft's interim URL-rewrite mitigations were later bypassed by the OWASSRF technique.
vulns.affected: Exchange Server 2013, 2016 and 2019 before the November 2022 security updates
vulns.fixed: November 8, 2022 Exchange security updates (KB5019758)
vulns.mitigation: Apply the November 2022 (or later) Exchange updates; the September 2022 URL-rewrite rules alone are insufficient (bypassed by OWASSRF); disable remote PowerShell for non-admin users.

vulns.name: TabShell
vulns.product: PowerShell / Microsoft Exchange Server remote PowerShell
vulns.discoverer: Viettel Cyber Security researchers
vulns.summary: TabShell (CVE-2022-41076) is a PowerShell remoting sandbox escape: from the restricted runspace that Exchange exposes, an authenticated user can break out and run arbitrary cmdlets and code. Viettel chained it with OWASSRF (CVE-2022-41080) to get from an Exchange mailbox login to code execution on the server. Microsoft fixed it in December 2022 Patch Tuesday, and Viettel published the research and name later that month.
vulns.affected: Windows PowerShell / PowerShell 7 builds before the December 2022 updates; reached through Exchange remote PowerShell
vulns.fixed: December 13, 2022 Patch Tuesday updates (PowerShell) plus the November 2022 Exchange updates for OWASSRF
vulns.mitigation: Apply the December 2022 PowerShell updates and November 2022+ Exchange updates; disable remote PowerShell for non-admin users; Microsoft notes blocking TCP 5985/5986 limits attacks.

vulns.name: ToolShell
vulns.discoverer: Dinh Ho Anh Khoa (Viettel Cyber Security) at Pwn2Own Berlin 2025; chain named and reproduced by Code White GmbH; mass exploitation found by Eye Security
vulns.summary: ToolShell abuses SharePoint's ToolPane.aspx endpoint: an authentication bypass (CVE-2025-49706) plus unsafe deserialization (CVE-2025-49704) give unauthenticated code execution. Attackers used it to drop spinstall0.aspx and steal ASP.NET machine keys, which let them forge signed ViewState payloads and keep access even after patching. CVE-2025-53770 and CVE-2025-53771 were assigned for patch bypasses of the July 2025 fixes.
vulns.affected: SharePoint Server Subscription Edition, 2019 and 2016 (on-premises only; SharePoint Online not affected)
vulns.fixed: July 2025 emergency updates: KB5002768 (Subscription Edition), KB5002754 + KB5002753 (2019), KB5002760 + KB5002759 (2016)
vulns.mitigation: Install the July 2025 updates, enable AMSI in Full Mode with Defender, then rotate ASP.NET machine keys and run iisreset on every SharePoint server; disconnect from the internet if AMSI cannot be enabled.

vulns.name: ShellTorch
vulns.discoverer: Idan Levcovich, Gal Elbaz and Guy Kaplan (Oligo Security)
vulns.summary: ShellTorch is a chain of TorchServe issues. The management API listens on all interfaces with no authentication by default, model URLs are not restricted, so a remote model can be fetched (SSRF, CVE-2023-43654), and SnakeYAML deserialization (CVE-2022-1471) is reachable from a model config. Together they let a remote attacker upload a malicious model and run code on AI model-serving servers.
vulns.affected: TorchServe 0.3.0 through 0.8.1 (including default AWS/Google deep learning containers)
vulns.fixed: TorchServe 0.8.2
vulns.mitigation: Upgrade to TorchServe 0.8.2+; bind management_address to 127.0.0.1; set allowed_urls to trusted model sources.
